To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the non-polar a-plane and semi-polar m-plane InGaN–Ga N quantum wells are more suitable for the high-power laser applications than the c-plane ones because of the vanishment of the internal electric field and large optical matrix elements.

the average hole effective masses along the wave vector are substantially reduced for the non-polarity and semi-polarity cases, which leads to the enhancement of the optical matrix elements and the gain.
non-polar and semipolar InGaN quantum wells exhibit a substantially larger optical gain than c-plane quantum wells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the multiband effective mass theory for non-polar and semipolar nitride quantum well structures and the calculation of their electronic band structures, optical matrix elements, and optical gain spectra.
the electronic and optical characteristics of nitride-based quantum well structures, with particular emphasis on non-polar and semipolar structures.
the electronic structure and optical gain of non-polar, semi-polar, and c-plane InGaN–AlGaN quantum wells for light-emitting devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
non-polar and semipolar nitride quantum-well structures are promising for high-efficiency light-emitting diode devices.
the non-polar a-plane and semi-polar m-plane InGaN–Ga N quantum well structures are promising for high efficiency light-emitting diodes and lasers.
the non-polar a-plane InGaN–GaNs quantum wells would be the most favorable structure for the realization of the high efficiency blue-green light emitters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
non-polar and (0 0 -1) semi-polar nitrides would be the promising candidates for the nitride-based optoelectronic devices.
non-polar and semipolar nitrides would be the most promising materials for the next generation nitride-based optoelectronic devices.
non-polar and semipolar nitride semiconductor structures are promising for the development of high-efficiency nitride semiconductor devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optical properties of nonpolar and semi-polarity nitride quantum well structures can be tailored by the crystal orientation.
the optical properties of nitride quantum-well structures are very sensitive to the crystal polar angle θ.
the non-polar (a- or m-plane) and semi-polar quantum-well structures are more favorable for optoelectronic device applications.
